summary.en: Define safe natural and alternate orders, including explicit tie breakers.
summary.bn: স্বাভাবিক ক্রম আর আলাদা সর্টিং নিয়ম লেখো, আর মান সমান হলে কী হবে তা ঠিক করো।

notes: All programs use Java 17 APIs and language rules.

sections.title: Use the sign rather than a particular integer
Trace the first key, then the tie breaker
Give each report a named policy
Check zero results and reversal placement
Comparator chains are available in Java 17
Turn ranking rules into explicit comparisons

examples.title: Sort by natural roll order
examples.explanationHtml: Passing null asks List.sort to use the elements’ natural Comparable order.

examples.title: Rank by marks and resolve ties
examples.explanationHtml: Roll 7 leads with 90. Rolls 3 and 12 share 80, so ascending roll orders that pair.

examples.title: See why subtraction is unsafe
examples.explanationHtml: The extreme int subtraction wraps around. Integer.compare preserves the mathematical ordering.

practice.title: Rank a class
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..30) then n pairs roll (1..999) and mark (0..100). Rolls are unique. Sort by descending mark then ascending roll. Print [roll:mark, ...], or []. No prompt.
hints: Reverse the mark comparator before adding the roll tie breaker.

practice.title: Order short words
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..30) then lowercase ASCII words. Print a bracketed list by increasing length, then lexical order. Keep duplicates. No prompt.
hints: Chain length with natural String order.

practice.title: Find a broken comparison
practice.statementHtml: A comparator returns 1 for every unequal pair and 0 otherwise. Explain which law fails.
practice.answerHtml: Swapping two unequal inputs still returns positive. Sign reversal fails, so each value claims to follow the other. Use a real key comparison.

practice.title: Choose the location of a policy
practice.statementHtml: A class has natural roll order. A report needs descending marks. Should compareTo change?
practice.answerHtml: Keep roll as the documented natural order. Supply a separate report comparator for marks and a tie breaker. Other natural-order clients remain predictable.
hints: Separate a class convention from a report choice.

quiz.prompt: Which student comes first under the natural roll order?
quiz.explanation: Natural comparison uses roll, not mark.

quiz.prompt: How does descending mark with ascending roll break the 80-mark tie?
quiz.explanation: Only the mark comparator is reversed; the roll comparator stays ascending.

quiz.prompt: How does overflow change subtraction compared with Integer.compare?
quiz.explanation: The subtraction overflows to positive one, but the safe comparison returns negative one.

quiz.prompt: Where is a natural order normally defined?
options: In compareTo on the element class
quiz.explanation: Comparable attaches a default ordering policy to the element type.

quiz.prompt: Which comparator result means the left argument comes first?
What does thenComparing do after unequal primary keys?
quiz.explanation: The secondary key is consulted only for a primary tie.

quiz.prompt: What does reversed at the end of a full chain reverse?
options: Every ordering decision in the chain
quiz.explanation: Reversing the complete comparator reverses its overall order.

quiz.prompt: What should a comparison do to its arguments?
quiz.explanation: Comparison should give a stable relation without side effects.

quiz.prompt: What does TreeSet do when comparison returns zero?
options: Treats the elements as the same set entry
quiz.explanation: Ordering equivalence defines membership for the tree set.

quiz.prompt: When is stable list sorting useful?
options: When comparator ties should preserve previous relative order
When all elements must be unique
When keys may change during comparison
quiz.explanation: Stability preserves input order among elements considered equivalent.

keyPoints.bn: Comparable ক্লাসের স্বাভাবিক ক্রম ঠিক করে।

keyPoints.en: Comparator supplies an outside ordering policy.
keyPoints.bn: Comparator দিয়ে বাইরের আলাদা সর্টিং নিয়ম দেওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: Comparison results are interpreted by sign.
keyPoints.bn: তুলনার ফলে ধনাত্মক, ঋণাত্মক বা শূন্য হওয়াটাই দরকারি।

keyPoints.en: Compare numeric keys without subtracting them.
keyPoints.bn: সংখ্যা তুলতে বিয়োগ না করে compare মেথড ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: Tie breakers make ranking requirements explicit.
keyPoints.bn: দুই মান সমান হলে পরের মান দিয়ে ক্রম ঠিক করো।

examQuestions.question: Compare Comparable and Comparator for student ranking.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Comparable supplies one natural order inside Student. Comparator supplies external alternatives such as descending marks with ascending roll. Both return a sign and must obey ordering laws.

examQuestions.question: Explain why marks-only TreeSet ordering can lose students.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Two different students with equal marks compare as zero. TreeSet considers them the same entry. Include the intended identity tie breaker or use a list when duplicates should remain.

examQuestions.question: Why is Integer.compare safer than a-b?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Subtraction may overflow and produce the wrong sign. Integer.compare compares values without computing their potentially overflowing difference.
